decision.detail: I push the duvet off. My feet hit the carpet, cold, the way they always do at six in the Hearthside. I reach over the nightstand. The envelope is there, cream-colored, the Pittsburgh postmark still wet-looking. I slide my thumb under the flap. I pull the receipt out. I read the line she copied. 'I know that voice. Play it again.' I read it a second time. I put the paper back in the envelope. I put the envelope back on the nightstand. I stand. I put my weight on both feet. The radio is still going in the hallway. The van did its thing. I am standing.
decision.intention: I will board the coach this morning and be at my sister's door in Pittsburgh by noon Wednesday. The van is booked. The hallway is the one with the water stain on the third step. The couch goes in. I am there. That is the whole of today and the whole of Wednesday. The envelope stays on the nightstand. I did not call her. I did not make it into a thing. I read the line. I put it down. The couch moves. I move with it.
decision.words: (quiet, to the room, to no one) Yeah. I'll be there.

You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
